blocks.content: Python iterators are objects that allow us to iterate over the iterables (lists, sets, tuples, etc.) and get data one at a time.
Iterators provide __iter__() and __next__() methods with which we can create our own custom loops.

items: __next__() - accesses the next data from an iterable

blocks.content:
1class Numbers:
2    def __iter__(self):
3        self.num = 1
4        return self
5
6    def __next__(self):
7        if self.num <= 5:
8            temp = self.num
9            self.num += 1
10            return temp
11        else:
12            raise StopIteration
13
14
15obj = iter(Numbers())
16
17for o in obj:
18    print(o)
Here, we've created a class, and inside the class, there are two methods __iter__() and __next__().

items: is called when we create an object of iterable
returns the next value starting from num = 1 to 5
if num is greater than 5, the StopIteration exception will stop the execution.

blocks.content: Hence, we can successfully implement a loop using an iterator.
